sections.title: Advanced Understanding of Line Graphs
sections.content: At Level 2, a line graph may contain two or more lines representing different companies, products, or categories. Questions usually involve comparison, percentage change, averages, and total calculations.

sections.title: Comparing Two or More Lines
sections.content: When two lines are given, read the values for each category carefully. Compare year by year and calculate the difference. If the lines meet at a point, it means both values are equal in that period.

sections.title: Rupees Based Comparative Example
sections.content: Suppose Company A earns 40000 rupees and Company B earns 35000 rupees in 2022. The difference is 5000 rupees. If in 2023 A earns 50000 and B earns 45000, both increased by 10000 rupees.

sections.title: Percentage Increase and Decrease
sections.content: To find percentage increase, divide the increase by the original value and multiply by 100. For example, increase from 40000 to 50000 is 10000. 10000 divided by 40000 times 100 equals 25 percent.

sections.title: Average Based Questions
sections.content: To find average over several years, add all values and divide by the number of years. This is commonly asked in exams.

sections.title: Combined Total Calculation
sections.content: If total of two companies is asked, first calculate individual totals and then add them together.

sections.title: Common Errors
sections.content: Students often calculate percentage using the new value instead of the original value. Always use the base year value for percentage calculations.

tricks.title: Quick Comparison Trick
tricks.explanation: First find the difference, then check what percent it is of the base value.
tricks.example: 50000 and 40000 differ by 10000, which is 25 percent of 40000.

tricks.title: Middle Value Average Trick
tricks.explanation: If numbers are close to each other, the middle value can be taken as approximate average.

tricks.title: Ratio Method
tricks.explanation: Convert large numbers into simple ratio form for easy comparison.

tricks.title: Total Difference Shortcut
tricks.explanation: If yearly difference is constant, multiply the difference by number of years.

tricks.title: Net Growth Shortcut
tricks.explanation: If total growth from first to last year is asked, subtract first year from last year directly.

tricks.title: Identify Highest Growth Year
tricks.explanation: Find year with maximum difference from previous year.
tricks.example: Increase of 15000 is higher than increase of 10000.

tricks.title: Intersection Point Trick
tricks.explanation: If two lines cross, their values are equal at that point.

tricks.title: Fast Percentage Estimation
tricks.explanation: If increase is one fourth of base value, percentage is 25 percent.

tricks.title: Step by Step Method
tricks.explanation: Read values carefully, calculate difference, then percentage if required.
tricks.example: First find change from 35000 to 42000, then calculate percentage.
